done_when: From the second blocked cold-read or review round on an item, forge next and close tell the coordinator to stop and ask the owner, listing every round's findings, and the shipped coordinator guide says to settle the missing rule one question at a time before the next round; new repos get it at init and existing repos on upgrade

known.title: Not done: From the second blocked cold-read or review round on an item, forge next and close tell the coordinator to stop and ask the owner,
Remote hard stops hide the required resolution step
Third-round output gives conflicting instructions about who decides

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. After a third blocked review triggers a hard stop, a remote item with no local worktree returns the new owner advice here before reaching the `state.stop` branch at lines 915–925. `forge next` says to send a focused round but omits the hard-stop question and the required `forge close --resolve` step. `close.check_stop` refuses that round until a choice is recorded. The new remote test covers two rounds, before this conflict occurs.
findings.title: Remote hard stops hide the required resolution step

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. With three distinct blocking findings in one area, all scored Harm 1 or 2, close prints the new instruction to ask the owner, then its hard-stop question says to settle the choice yourself and tell the owner afterward (`review.stop_question` uses `score.who`). The shipped guide repeats both instructions at lines 1472–1477 and 1510–1515. This reachable third-round case leaves the coordinator with opposite directions about whether to ask the owner before another round.
findings.title: Third-round output gives conflicting instructions about who decides

why: Coordinators keep sending workers back round after round when a cold read or review finds a new problem each time, instead of stopping to settle the missing rule with the owner
